nodes.content: Design an SSD-backed key-value store that limits write amplification under long-lived snapshots without sacrificing crash consistency.
requirements: Reduce total host-written bytes by 30% versus leveled LSM compaction under identical update-heavy workloads.
Preserve snapshot isolation and acknowledged writes across crashes; keep p99 reads within 10% of baseline.

nodes.content: Isolate snapshot-pinned versions in indexed immutable segments; compact active versions, fsync WAL before acknowledgment, and atomically publish manifests.
What pinning granularity reduces copied bytes without pushing p99 point reads beyond 110% of the leveled LSM baseline?
Under hour-long snapshots, 4-MiB version-segment pinning cuts host-written bytes ≥30% versus leveled LSM, with p99 reads ≤1.10× baseline.
Benchmark 1-, 4-, and 16-MiB snapshot-pinned segments against leveled LSM under hour-long snapshots; compare host-written bytes and p99 reads.
Run UpdateBench-60 (80% updates, hour-long snapshots) comparing 1-, 4-, 16-MiB segments against leveled LSM; measure host-written bytes and p99 reads.
UpdateBench-60: 4-MiB pinning wrote 68 GiB versus leveled LSM’s 100 GiB; p99 reads were 1.08× baseline.
Select 4-MiB snapshot-pinned segments: UpdateBench-60 met the write-byte reduction target with p99 reads below the 1.10× limit.
Implement selected 4-MiB pinning; run CrashBench-4M power-cut injections around WAL fsync and manifest publication, checking acknowledged writes and snapshot isolation.
4-MiB pinning patch and CrashBench-4M report covering WAL and manifest fault points, acknowledged-write recovery, and snapshot-visibility checks.
Rerun UpdateBench-60 on the 4-MiB pinning patch with WAL fsync; compare host-written bytes and p99 reads against leveled LSM.
With WAL fsync enabled, UpdateBench-60 measured 77 GiB versus leveled LSM’s 100 GiB; p99 reads were 1.08× baseline.
One-MiB pinning with fsynced WAL group commits will write ≤70 GiB versus 100 GiB baseline, with p99 reads ≤1.10×.
Run UpdateBench-60 with 1-MiB pins and 2-ms fsynced WAL group commits; compare host-written GiB and p99 reads against leveled LSM.
UpdateBench-60 with 1-MiB pins and fsynced group commits wrote 69 GiB versus 100 GiB baseline; p99 reads were 1.09×.
How should recovery reconstruct snapshot pins after a crash between WAL fsync and atomic manifest publication?
WAL-log snapshot registrations; inject CrashBench-1M cuts after WAL fsync, before manifest publication; verify recovered pins preserve visibility.
CrashBench-1M: 10,000 injected crashes recovered all acknowledged writes and WAL-registered snapshot pins, with zero visibility violations.
Separate values into an append-only MVCC log, compact only key indexes, and fsync commits before publishing snapshot-visible index roots.
Implement value-log MVCC; measure UpdateBench-60 host bytes and p99 versus LSM; fault-inject commits to verify durability and snapshot recovery.
Reuse CrashBench-1M recovery checks to compare 1-MiB pinning and value-log MVCC on UpdateBench-60 host bytes, p99 reads, and crashes.
UpdateBench-60 comparison report with host-written GiB, p99 reads, and CrashBench-1M recovery checks for both designs.
Recompute both designs’ UpdateBench-60 write-byte and p99 ratios from the report; inspect CrashBench-1M logs for recovery violations.
UpdateBench-60: value-log MVCC wrote 63 GiB versus 100 GiB baseline and 69 GiB pinning; p99 reads 1.06×, zero recovery violations.
Select value-log MVCC over 1-MiB pinning: 63 versus 69 GiB written, lower p99 reads, and zero recovery violations.
Implement selected value-log MVCC with snapshot-watermarked GC; fsync relocated values before publishing index roots and reclaiming old segments.
Value-log MVCC patch adds snapshot-watermarked GC, fsynced relocation, and atomic index-root publication; includes UpdateBench-60 and CrashBench-1M harnesses.
Under 24-hour snapshots, watermarked GC keeps value-log MVCC host writes ≤70% of leveled LSM and p99 reads ≤1.10×.
Run UpdateBench-24h on the value-log MVCC patch and leveled LSM; measure host-written GiB and p99 reads during watermarked GC.
UpdateBench-24h: value-log MVCC wrote 76 GiB versus leveled LSM’s 100 GiB; p99 reads reached 1.14× baseline during GC.
Profile UpdateBench-24h GC stalls; rerun with 80%-dead segment selection and 5-MiB/s relocation throttling, measuring host bytes and p99.
UpdateBench-24h with 80%-dead GC and 5-MiB/s throttling wrote 69 GiB versus 100 GiB baseline; p99 reads fell to 1.09×.
Use snapshot-aware tiered LSM runs with fsynced WAL commits and Bloom-filtered indexes to reduce compaction writes while bounding reads.
Can snapshot-aware tiering cap point-read run probes without exceeding 70 GiB written on UpdateBench-24h?
Replacing value-log GC, four-run snapshot-aware tiering should write ≤70 GiB with ≤4 probes and ≤1.10× p99 on UpdateBench-24h.
Extend the value-log patch’s harness for four-run tiering on UpdateBench-24h; compare writes and p99 against both GC configurations, measure probes.
UpdateBench-24h: four-run tiering wrote 66 GiB versus 100 GiB baseline, but p99 reads reached 1.13×.
Using the value-log patch’s harness, cache four-run indexes to address 1.13× p99; rerun UpdateBench-24h measuring writes, probes, and p99.
UpdateBench-24h with cached four-run indexes wrote 67 GiB versus 100 GiB baseline; maximum probes were four, p99 reads 1.08×.
With a 64-MiB index cache, four-run tiering should sustain ≤70 GiB written, ≤4 probes, and ≤1.10× p99 on UpdateBench-24h.
Validate 64-MiB index-cache tiering across UpdateBench-24h seeds; measure host-written GiB, maximum run probes, p99 reads, and crash recovery.
Adapt the value-log harness for 64-MiB cached tiering; run five UpdateBench-24h seeds and CrashBench-1M, measuring host-written GiB, probes, p99, recovery.
Across five UpdateBench-24h seeds, cached tiering wrote 66–69 GiB versus 100 GiB baseline; ≤4 probes, ≤1.09× p99, zero crash violations.
Extend the value-log patch’s CrashBench-1M harness for 64-MiB cached-tier publication faults; rerun UpdateBench-24h after recovery, measuring bytes, probes, p99.
After CrashBench-1M publication cuts, UpdateBench-24h wrote 68 GiB and probed ≤4 runs, but cold-cache p99 reached 1.16× baseline.
Reject cached tiering despite ≤1.09× warm p99: post-crash p99 reaches 1.16×; retain throttled value-log MVCC (69 GiB, 1.09×).
Implement 80%-dead, 5-MiB/s value-log GC; run CrashBench-24h on relocation crashes, checking acknowledged writes and snapshot isolation.
Throttled value-log MVCC patch with 80%-dead GC, 5-MiB/s relocation cap, and CrashBench-24h relocation-fault report.
Can persisted run-index hints bring tiering’s post-crash p99 below 1.10× without raising host writes above 70 GiB?
Reuse n48’s crash-testing setup to fault persisted tiered-run hint publication; compare post-crash p99 and UpdateBench-24h writes against throttled MVCC.
Persisted tiered-run hints cut post-crash p99 to 1.07× baseline; UpdateBench-24h wrote 69 GiB versus leveled LSM’s 100 GiB.
Use immutable Bε-tree batches with snapshot-aware version chains and fsynced commit records, avoiding full-level rewrites while indexing reads.
Prototype immutable Bε-tree batches; compare UpdateBench-24h writes and p99 against leveled LSM, then inject commit and snapshot-recovery crashes.
Adapt n27’s benchmark harness and n48’s crash-fault tests for Bε-tree batches; measure UpdateBench-24h writes, p99 reads, and recovery.
Bε-tree prototype and UpdateBench-24h/CrashBench-24h comparison report covering host-written GiB, p99 reads, and acknowledged-write recovery.
Compare Bε-tree report’s writes, post-crash p99, and snapshot recovery against persisted-hint tiering’s 69 GiB and 1.07× p99.
UpdateBench-24h: Bε-tree wrote 65 GiB versus 100 GiB baseline; post-crash p99 was 1.05×, with zero snapshot or durability violations.
Select Bε-tree over persisted-hint tiering: 65 versus 69 GiB written, 1.05× versus 1.07× post-crash p99, no recovery violations.
Harden selected Bε-tree prototype: fsync commit records before acknowledgment, atomically publish batch roots, and fault-test snapshot-version pruning.
Hardened Bε-tree patch adds fsynced commits, atomic batch-root publication, snapshot-safe pruning, and CrashBench-24h fault tests.
